rule: Two border lines (1 and 2) meet at a 0 corner. If the 1-line is vertical, turn the grid 90 degrees CCW. Read the two 2-thick lanes nearest the 1-line first. Within each lane, read the blocks nearest the 2-line first. Stack the blocks vertically as they appear, each centred in a strip as wide as the longest block.
scope: Original two-lane fixtures preserved. Random scenes mix 2..4 lanes; explicit num_lanes supports 2..5. Added lanes are a synthetic extrapolation of the same reading rule. Each lane has 2..5 blocks of even lengths 2..8, with optional asymmetric accent patterns. All eight border orientations are supported; vertical 1-lines are normalized by a counter-clockwise rotation. Output height capped at 30; normalized input width up to 30. Exact requested width and lane count honored, with bounded rejection and no canned fallback.
constraints: Normalized frame has 3*lane_count+2 rows, width <=30, and a trailing background margin.
Blocks are rectangular, two rows high, even in width, and contain neither 0 nor background 8.
Lanes and blocks are separated; corner and full border lines uniquely specify reading order.
At least two block widths occur in random scenes, requiring nontrivial centering.
Total block count <=15 keeps output height <=30.
known_limitations: The orientation convention for vertical 1-lines (always turn CCW, never flip blocks) follows the verified solver. Orientations with the 1-line at the bottom of the normalised frame and a horizontal input are not in the fixtures, so their reading follows the solver's distance-based convention.
Gap size and initial offset are fixed at the values seen in every fixture.
More than two lanes is a synthetic mechanism extension, not an observed original example.
Background 8 and border cue colours 0/1/2 remain fixed.
Blocks have two rows and even lengths; arbitrary backgrounds, odd lengths and holes are not generated.
Difficult requested configurations may raise after 2000 attempts; no fixed substitute is returned.
billing: Claude Max CLI; API credentials excluded; no API fallback
